Halikṣṇa or Halīkṣṇa is mentioned as one of the victims at the aśvamedha (‘horse sacrifice’) in the yajurveda Saṃhitās. The commentator Mahīdhara thinks that it is a kind of lion, Sāyaṇa that a green Caṭaka bird or a lion (tṛṇa-hiṃsa) is meant. In the Atharvaveda Halīkṣṇa seems to be some particular intestine, but Weber thinks it may mean ‘gall.’
